Definition: Abimelek, the name of two Philistine kings and of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Abimelech is the name of two Philistine kings of Gerar — one who takes Sarah and is warned by God in a dream, one who watches Isaac’s wells and makes a covenant with him. It is also the name of Gideon’s son, who murders his seventy brothers, is made king of Shechem, and dies when a woman drops a millstone on his head.
TheologicalSignificance: The same name covers a king God warns in mercy and a son who murders his way to a throne. I believe the two Abimelechs show me the two roads a name can take: one listens when God speaks in a dream, and the other listens to no one — and the end of each road is very different.
